performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body:
## Codex review — correctness, performance, and structure

I reviewed this at `8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0`. Overall, the incremental core has a better safety story than I expected: the sparse normalization path is parity-run against the global path throughout the editing suite, the item persistence ordering/fallback tests are substantive, and identity-preserving splices plus compositional statics are coherent optimizations. The branch builds cleanly and the complete local `@runtest` suite passes.

I did find several correctness issues in the newer UI/persistence plumbing, plus one performance claim that needs narrowing.

### Correctness findings

1. **[P1] Persisted outline paths are not unique, and some valid labels cannot round-trip through the ad-hoc encoding.** [`label_path`/`resolve_path`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/app/sidebar/OutlineTree.re#L340-L376) use only display labels and `resolve_path` selects the first match. Two separated test runs both create a container labeled `tests`; a saved pin under the second group resolves into the first group and then fails. Duplicate definitions have the same problem. Collapse is worse: [`my_path = path @ [n.o_label]`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/app/sidebar/OutlineSidebar.re#L372-L380) means collapsing one top-level `tests` group collapses every top-level `tests` group. In addition, [`write_pins`/`read_pins`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/view/ScratchPersist.re#L69-L122) use spaces, `/`, and newlines as unescaped delimiters; a backticked definition name containing a space is silently discarded on reload. Use a derived sexp/JSON value and a durable component such as `{kind, label, same-label occurrence}` (or a source/item anchor that survives text reload). Please test duplicate names, two disjoint test groups, and a backticked name with spaces.

2. **[P1] Caret/pin/collapse restoration state is module-global and not tagged with the document it belongs to.** [`pending_caret` and `pending_pins`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/view/ScratchPersist.re#L65-L88) are singleton refs. `read_caret` leaves the previous value intact for a missing or malformed key ([lines 124–143](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/view/ScratchPersist.re#L124-L143)), while `RestoreCaret` applies the point to whichever slide is current when the queued action executes ([ScratchMode lines 773–803](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/view/ScratchMode.re#L773-L803)). A hydration/mode-switch race can therefore move the wrong editor. Collapse and transient pins are keyed only by slide name, not `(prefix, name)`, and [`read_collapse(None)` does not clear the old same-name entry](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/view/ScratchPersist.re#L90-L103), so Scratch and Documentation slides with the same name bleed state. Put this state in the slide/workspace model, or at minimum key/tag every value and restore action with a document key and verify it against the current document before applying. Clear pending state before every read.

3. **[P1] `CaretReveal` leaks one scroll handler per cold reveal and can reuse another editor's geometry during a burst.** Every cold anchor calls [`attach_scroll_listener`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/util/CaretReveal.re#L92-L104), but no old handler is removed. The browser retains every old `geom` closure and invokes all of them on each scroll. Separately, `published` contains only `(row, row_height)`, and the hot path accepts any connected cached container ([lines 269–289](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/util/CaretReveal.re#L269-L289)). Moving from one stacked cell/header to another within 500 ms can combine the new row with the old editor's `editor_top`, causing a wrong scroll until verification heals it. Maintain one removable listener per active container and include an editor/cell identity in the published geometry; identity change should force a cold anchor. This module currently has no test coverage, so a small DOM-level listener-count and cross-cell reanchor test would pay for itself.

### Performance findings and measurements

4. **[P2] Per-item persistence pays off, but the PR description overstates the end-to-end autosave result.** [`save_current`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/8e0c9d7dbc7323e5edee6ea00c0f91c5db7f4ff0/src/web/view/ScratchPersist.re#L288-L389) writes changed items and then serializes/writes the whole text-backed slide on every content-changing pause. On this machine, the branch's `SerBench` harness measured text printing at **11 ms for Mega 1k** and **27 ms for Mega 4k**; by comparison, whole-segment sexp+string at 4k was **335/351/353 ms**, so the move away from whole-zipper sexp is clearly worthwhile. But autosave still has an O(document) ~27 ms main-thread floor in addition to the claimed 3–10 ms item write. I would keep the item store primary and move the schema-insurance text blob to an idle/rate-limited policy (plus a page-hide flush), or serialize it in a worker. At minimum, revise “writes only the edited item” in the PR description.

5. Current headless statics figures also support the broad direction but show why the exact workload matters: `LabelBench` measured Mega 4k cold `DefStatics.calc` at **872 ms / 891 items**, then a surgical one-item edit at **56 ms / 16 items analyzed**; the full incremental `init_compositional_term` path was **58 ms**. That is a large improvement over a cold pass, but it is not literally one analyzed item for this dependency shape. These are Node/headless numbers, not browser interaction latency; the browser keystroke/view/GC claims still need a reproducible UI harness.

### Structure recommendation

The split from the old ~4.7k-line file is useful, but `ScratchMode.re` is still 2,752 lines and the feature now depends on shared globals in `ScratchPersist`, `ScratchMode`, `CaretReveal`, `CodeWithStatics`, and `DefStatics`. The state-leak findings above are symptoms of an unclear ownership boundary.

I would make the core abstraction a **multi-slide editor workspace**, not “scratch mode”:

- `SlideDeck`: document identity, names/current slide, hydration, persistence namespace, dormant state.
- `EditorWorkspace`: master editor + optional stack, focus/navigation, splicing/restructure, projected statics.
- `OutlineController`: outline tree plus modeled pins/collapse/menu state, keyed by document identity.
- Thin Scratch and Documentation adapters: defaults, labels, persistence prefix, and whether derivation slides are offered.

Outline/stack is then an editor capability consumed by both modes; Scratch and Documentation stop being the place where core editor lifetime is defined. I would also move the remaining module-global mutable refs into explicit non-historic workspace/controller state or lifecycle-owned services. That is a larger cleanup, but it directly prevents the prefix/slide/race classes above and makes future Project/editor reuse much less risky.

### Suggested merge posture

I do not see a reason to discard the main incremental work: sparse regrout parity, compositional statics, item storage, chunked measurement/view, and identity-preserving splices are individually defensible. I would fix findings 1–3 before merging, narrow or change the autosave claim/policy, and keep #2480's consumer flip separate until its protocol recovery issues are resolved.
